Evidence: backend/app/ml/dataset_loader.py loads 12 CSVs from data/synthetic_enterprise/; CIC-IDS2017 PortScan flow dataset is supported but primary risk model uses synthetic topology.
Why It Matters: Real-world enterprise environments exhibit complex noise, multi-cloud IAM entanglements, and unpredictable user behaviors not captured in synthetic schemas.
Impact: Model could suffer distribution shift, leading to higher false-positive rates (observed at 68.4% on holdout at calibrated theta=0.32) in live production.
Recommended Improvement: Train and benchmark against production Zeek/Suricata/EDR streams; incorporate active feedback loop to adaptively re-weight features.

Evidence: frontend/src/App.tsx is 10,873 lines long, containing state, routing, UI rendering, canvas handlers, and 12 dashboard views in a single file.
Why It Matters: Violates single-responsibility principle; makes concurrent frontend collaboration difficult and increases risk of regressions during UI updates.
Impact: Prevents modular component-level testing (e.g. Vitest/React Testing Library); limits tree-shaking and component reusability.
Recommended Improvement: Decompose App.tsx into dedicated view directories (views/AttackGraph.tsx, views/Optimizer.tsx, etc.) and adopt Zustand/Redux Toolkit for global state.

Weakness: Simulated Blockchain Anchoring Under Offline RPC
Evidence: backend/app/audit/blockchain_client.py falls back to mock transaction hashes when Ethereum Sepolia JSON-RPC is unreachable or wallet unconfigured.
Why It Matters: External judges or auditors evaluating the platform without live internet/Sepolia access might question whether blockchain integration is genuine or mocked.
Impact: Audit integrity relies on local SHA-256 hash chain and Merkle proofs rather than decentralized consensus when running in offline/airgapped environments.
Recommended Improvement: Bundle a local Anvil/Hardhat containerized EVM node in Docker compose for 100% genuine local on-chain transaction execution and block explorer validation.

Weakness: Hardcoded Business Continuity Digital Twin Workflows
Evidence: backend/app/business/twin.py defines 7 static workflows (WF-001 through WF-007) with fixed downtime financial cost rates and SLA thresholds.
Why It Matters: Enterprise organizations operate dynamic microservice architectures with changing revenue impacts and hundreds of inter-service dependencies.
Impact: Limits out-of-the-box adaptability for non-financial organizations without manual code or configuration modifications.
Recommended Improvement: Expose dynamic CMDB / ServiceNow / Datadog Service Catalog REST connector allowing SecOps to dynamically sync live business service mappings.

Evidence: backend/app/graph/engine.py find_attack_paths() enumerates multi-hop paths between all compromised nodes and crown jewels.
Why It Matters: All-paths enumeration in densely connected cyclic graphs has exponential worst-case computational complexity O(V! / (V-k)!).
Impact: May cause pipeline latency spikes or memory pressure if evaluated on massive unpartitioned enterprise topologies (>50,000 nodes).
Recommended Improvement: Implement Yen k-shortest paths with k=10 pruning, or hierarchical graph partitioning (subnet/enclave aggregation) prior to host-level path traversal.

Weakness: In-Memory User Store Default in Development
Evidence: backend/app/security/auth.py uses an in-memory user repository seeded with default credentials (admin/admin, analyst/analyst).
Why It Matters: Default credentials in development environments can pose security risks if deployed to production without environment overrides.
Impact: Server restarts clear dynamically created user accounts unless persisted to PostgreSQL/SQLite.
Recommended Improvement: Enforce mandatory database-backed user persistence and disable default credentials when ENVIRONMENT=production.

Weakness: Limited Real Disruption Containment Execution (Safe Guardrail)
Evidence: backend/app/optimization/solver.py plans actions with status APPROVAL_REQUIRED, intentionally forbidding automated disruptive firewall cuts.
Why It Matters: Hackathon judges expecting an aggressive auto-blocking SOAR tool might misinterpret safe enterprise guardrails as missing execution.
Impact: System acts as a decision-support and simulation platform rather than an autonomous active defense agent executing unsanctioned network outages.
Recommended Improvement: Document this explicitly as a core enterprise architectural feature (Separation of Concerns & Human-in-the-Loop Governance) rather than a limitation.
